claims.text: The local source slice models five rows for the 64 Mario Stadium Best Photo Contest: Koffing 101, Charmander 102, Articuno 103, Squirtle 104, and Chansey 105.

Bulbapedia's illustration-contests page says TV Tokyo variety show 64 Mario Stadium held a Best Photo Contest in May 1999, entrants could submit postcards with photos printed from Pokemon Snap Sticker Stations, winners received producer calls to verify game save data, and only 15 of each card were distributed to each winner.

The contest converted Pokemon Snap player photographs into reprints from Expansion Pack and Mystery of the Fossils, making the route a media bridge between Nintendo 64 play, television, postcards, and TCG objects.

Card pages describe a camera graphic where an expansion symbol normally appears; some pages also note bottom-right Best Photo Contest Winners Prize Card text. These are identification rails, not authentication substitutes.
This release matters because children were not just consuming Pokemon images; they were making them. The apparatus let a player camera become a card face.

Agents should preserve 64 Mario Stadium route, Pokemon Snap photo-credit identity, camera-symbol print, 15-copy winner distribution context, row 101-105 identity, and Base/Fossil/reprint non-equivalence before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: 64 Mario Stadium Best Photo Contest — when a player's camera became the card
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the cleanest answers to why the catalog has to care about assembly. These cards are not famous because Koffing, Charmander, Articuno, Squirtle, and Chansey were newly invented. They are famous because a child or player saw them through Pokemon Snap, printed the shot, mailed it into a television-show contest, had save data checked, and received a tiny run of cards where the photograph replaced the usual illustration. The card face is a record of someone loving Pokemon actively enough to frame it.
